$comment: CTL-042 — scheduled workflows that are deliberately NOT active.
Read by scripts/check-scheduled-workflows-active.py. Every entry needs a
Jira key AND a reason; a bare marker is itself a failure, and an entry for
a workflow that has since been re-enabled is a STALE exception and fails
the check outright — a list containing things that no longer apply is a
list nobody reads.
DECIDED 2026-08-09 by Luisa. Four workflows were found dark since mid-June.
Two were re-enabled (anomaly-detect, mutation-testing) and are deliberately
absent from this file — listing an active workflow here is an error. The
two below are excepted with reasons rather than re-enabled.
TWO KINDS OF ENTRY LIVE HERE, AND ONLY ONE IS MEANT TO PERSIST (BUGS-102).
DELIBERATELY OFF — a registered workflow someone decided to disable. It
stays until that decision is revisited. Both 2026-08-09 entries are this.
NOT YET REGISTERED — a workflow ADDED in the same PR. Until the file is
merged somewhere GitHub indexes, the workflow does not exist to the API
and the check would otherwise fail the PR that puts it there. This kind
is SHORT-LIVED BY CONSTRUCTION: the moment it registers, the exception is
STALE and fails the build, which is what forces its removal rather than
leaving it as a permanent allowlist entry.
⚠️ REGISTRATION REQUIRES THE DEFAULT BRANCH (`main`). This note said the
opposite between 2026-08-14 10:34 and 2026-08-14 20:45, and the correction
matters because it changes how long an entry of the second kind must live.
The retracted claim: 'release-integrity.yml merged to DEVELOP at 10:33 UTC
and the API reported it state: active at 10:34:35, four promotes short of
main — so write this kind of entry expecting to delete it in the SAME
session you merge.' The inference does not hold: release-integrity.yml is
ALSO on main, beta and staging (v0.1.97-v0.1.99 promoted the same day), so
reaching the default branch is not excluded by that observation.
Measured directly on 2026-08-14 with routine-evidence.yml, which was on
develop and nowhere else. `gh api repos/luisa-sys/lyra/actions/workflows
--paginate` did not list it (41 workflows, and release-integrity.yml showed
`active` in the same response as a positive control), and `gh run list
--workflow=routine-evidence.yml` answered, verbatim:
HTTP 404: workflow routine-evidence.yml not found on the default branch
So an entry of the second kind lives until its workflow reaches `main` via
the normal promote chain — days, not seconds. It still goes STALE the moment
it registers and still must be DELETED rather than suppressed; what changed
is when to expect that, and therefore when its continued presence is a
finding rather than a normal in-flight state.
So an entry of the second kind that is still here once `main` carries its
workflow is itself a finding — either the promote never happened, or the
workflow registered and somebody suppressed the STALE failure instead of
deleting the line. Do not read it as 'still here after a day': a promote to
`main` legitimately takes longer than that, which is exactly what the
correction above is about.
WORKED EXAMPLE, start to finish (routine-evidence.yml, CTL-062, SEC-146).
Added to this file 2026-08-14 in PR #803 because the API reported no state
for it at all. It stayed unregistered through the merge to develop and
through the staging and beta promotes, and registered as `state: active`
immediately once `beta -> main` merged it onto the default branch. The check
then failed it as STALE on the very next run, and the line was deleted rather
than suppressed. That is the whole intended lifecycle, and it took one
session and four branches rather than the ninety seconds this file used to
claim.

.github/workflows/absent-secrets-probe.y.reason: NOT YET REGISTERED — the second kind of entry described above. Added 2026-08-17 in the same change that creates the workflow; GitHub does not index a schedule trigger until the file reaches the default branch, so CTL-042 would otherwise fail the very PR that puts it there. DELETE THIS LINE once it reaches `main` via the promote chain. ⚠️ Note deliberately NOT accompanied by a test asserting this entry exists — required-checks.yml had one, and on 2026-08-16 it deadlocked develop outright: keeping the exception failed CTL-042 on every PR while removing it failed that test, and there was no green state until a founder-signed-off assertion change. An entry that is short-lived by construction must not be pinned by anything.
.github/workflows/absent-secrets-probe.y.expires_when: absent-secrets-probe.yml is reported ACTIVE by the GitHub API

.github/workflows/affiliate-link-smoke.y.reason: Its last three scheduled runs FAILED before it went dark on 2026-06-16, so re-enabling it would put a known-red hourly job back on the board without fixing what it is reporting. Decided 2026-08-09 (Luisa): stay off until the failure is diagnosed. Re-enabling it is the fix; this exception is the placeholder, not the answer.

.github/workflows/auto-promote-to-stagin.reason: Weekly develop->staging auto-promote. SEC-98 made production change control manual-only and withdrew the fix-only auto-promote exception on 2026-07-23; an unattended promote sits awkwardly beside that even though staging is not production. Decided 2026-08-09 (Luisa): stay off. NOTE: CLAUDE.md's Deployment Pipeline section still describes this as auto-running Sunday 23:00 UTC — that line is now wrong and is corrected in this commit.
